extracted.intended_audience: general public, potential donors/supporters, journalists, whistleblowers and researchers interested in CMD's work
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, practices, and organizational commitments CMD uses to produce investigative watchdog journalism and maintain editorial independence and transparency. Covers methods (FOIA, original research), governance, funding disclosure, ethics, and dissemination/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth, award-winning investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Media and Democracy (CMD) is a nationally recognized watchdog that leads in-depth, award-winning investigations into the corruption that undermines our democracy, environment, and economic prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMD emphasizes long-form investigative work that uncovers corruption and distortion of law and democracy. Examples cited include exposing ALEC and investigations into ties between public officials and industry. Awards and media placements are presented as evidence of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research beyond the 24-hour news cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Our original research digs deeper than the 24-hour news cycle to answer and understand why and how special interests and dark money are reshaping American politics and elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should go beyond quick news reporting to provide deeper analysis and explanation of systems and motivations. The team focuses on documenting facts and revealing effects on communities across areas like climate change, education, workplace standards, and free speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public information requests / FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: CMD files more than 1,000 public information requests each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive use of public records and FOIA requests is a core investigative method. CMD lists FOIA experts on staff and highlights that such requests fuel national-impact stories (e.g., EPA Administrator ties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to litigate to defend the public’s right to know
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary, CMD litigates to defend that right and ensure those in power follow the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation is an operational tool to enforce transparency and access to government records; CMD states it brings lawsuits when required to obtain information or hold power to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document facts and reveal effects on communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our team focuses on documenting the facts and revealing the effects on communities and people in areas ranging from climate change and education to workplace standards and freedom of speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should connect documented facts to real-world impacts on communities, not only catalogue activities of special interests. This is emphasized as part of the research mission and differentiates their investigative approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of funding and donor disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: To promote transparency, CMD voluntarily discloses its major funders. CMD’s most recent 990 can be found here. Less than 10% of CMD’s annual revenues come from anonymous donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMD lists foundations and individuals who donated $5,000+ since Jan 1, 2020 and makes tax filings available. Voluntary disclosure of major funders is a stated organizational standard for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding limits and acceptance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept no grants from government agencies or for-profit corporations, except for CREDO, which makes donations to nonprofits based on votes by its activists and customers. Contributions from individuals and non-profit organizations are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMD sets boundaries on sources of funding to protect independence; exceptions are explicitly noted. This policy is presented as part of safeguarding editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and adherence to journalistic ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: CMD’s donors play no role in determining or reviewing CMD’s investigations and news coverage. We are committed to upholding high standards of fair and accurate journalism and follow the Code of Ethics provided by the Society for Professional Journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donor non-interference and explicit adherence to the SPJ Code of Ethics are core ethical commitments. This serves as a rule to avoid conflicts of interest and maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff expertise and multidisciplinary team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: CMD’s team includes researchers, data experts, FOIA experts, lawyers, and fact-checkers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation quality is supported by a team with specialized skills (legal, data, FOIA, fact-checking), indicating an expectation of rigorous methods and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dedicated publishing platforms and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: CMD’s groundbreaking exposés are featured on ExposedbyCMD.org. The watchdog also publishes SourceWatch, specialized investigative websites including ALECExposed.org, and its founding website PRWatch.org. We also partner with investigative writers at The Intercept and ProPublica to publish new reports and findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain multiple platforms and collaborate with other reputable investigative outlets to maximize reach and credibility. SourceWatch is described as an encyclopedia resource, indicating a commitment to archival and reference publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact orientation (measurable outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since CMD first exposed ALEC in 2011, more than 100 corporations have dropped ALEC, including Verizon, Ford, Coca-Cola, Wal‑Mart, General Electric, and Google.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations are expected to yield tangible public impact (e.g., corporate withdrawals, national debate). Impact and recognition (media amplification, awards) are presented as markers of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and awards as validation of quality
rubrics_metrics.description: CMD’s investigations have been recognized for their excellence and impact with awards such as the Sidney Award, the I.F. Stone Award, Professional Freedom and Responsibility Award, the 'Benny' from the Business Ethics Network, and local press honors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External awards, film features, and media placements (NYT, WaPo, POLITICO, Guardian, etc.) are cited as validation of standards and quality. Use of such recognition supports claims of credibility.
